comments.text:
Cenk Uygur is falsely claiming Israel “faked intelligence” about an Iranian assassination attempt on Donald Trump and has a “track record” of manipulating U.S. policy.
Let’s break down why these claims fall apart under even basic scrutiny.

1️⃣ Claim: “Netanyahu once gave false intelligence in the White House Situation Room.”

Reality:
Israel didn’t “fabricate” anything. Israeli intelligence assessments—like U.S. intelligence assessments—are analyses, not prophecies. They present scenarios, risks, and strategic options.

The idea that Israel walked into the Situation Room and said “near certain victory” or “Iran’s missile program could be destroyed in weeks” is not supported by any official transcript, memo, or verified leak.

Israel has consistently warned the U.S. about:

• Iran’s expanding ballistic missile program
• Iran’s destabilizing regional militias
• Iran’s nuclear ambitions


These warnings have been validated repeatedly by U.S. intelligence, the IAEA, and bipartisan congressional reports.

If anything, Israel has been more accurate than many Western agencies about Iran’s intentions.

---

2️⃣ Claim: “Israel said Iran wouldn’t retaliate if attacked.”

Reality:
Israel has never claimed Iran would simply sit quietly after a U.S. strike.
Israeli intelligence has always emphasized:

• Iran’s use of proxies (Hezbollah, Houthis, Iraqi militias)
• Iran’s cyber capabilities
• Iran’s willingness to retaliate asymmetrically


This is documented in years of Israeli MOD briefings and U.S. CENTCOM reports.

The idea that Israel told the U.S. “don’t worry, Iran won’t retaliate” is pure fiction.

---

3️⃣ Claim: “Israel said the Strait of Hormuz wouldn’t be threatened.”

Reality:
Israel has consistently warned that Iran does have the capability to disrupt the Strait of Hormuz.
This is not controversial—it’s widely acknowledged by:

• U.S. Navy Fifth Fleet
• International maritime security analysts
• The Department of Defense


The claim that Israel said the opposite is not supported anywhere in official documentation.

---

4️⃣ Claim: “Israel claimed bombing + riots would overthrow Iran’s regime.”

Reality:
Israel has never promoted a “bomb them and riots will topple the regime” strategy.
Israel’s actual documented position:

• Iran’s regime is deeply entrenched
• Internal uprisings are unpredictable
• Military pressure alone cannot guarantee regime collapse


This is exactly why Israel focuses on deterrence, covert operations, and preventing nuclear breakout, not fantasies about instant regime change.

The video’s claim that Israel “internally predicted massacres” contradicts decades of Israeli policy emphasizing avoiding civilian casualties and preventing regional destabilization.

---

5️⃣ Claim: “Israel faked intelligence about an Iranian assassination attempt on Trump.”

Reality:
Iran has a long, documented history of:

• Targeting U.S. officials
• Attempting assassinations abroad
• Conducting plots on American soil (DOJ charged Iranian agents in 2021 for attempting to assassinate a U.S. journalist)
• Threatening former U.S. presidents and officials explicitly


When Israel shares intelligence about Iranian threats, it is because Iran has repeatedly demonstrated intent and capability.
The idea that Israel “invented” a plot targeting Trump ignores Iran’s own public statements and past operations.

---

🇺🇸🇮🇱 Bottom Line

This video isn’t “exposing” anything.
It’s recycling old anti‑Israel talking points, stripping them of context, and presenting them as “proof” of manipulation.

Israel and the United States share intelligence because both nations face the same enemy:
a regime that funds terrorism, destabilizes the Middle East, and openly threatens American leaders.

Trying to paint Israel as the villain only helps one actor: Tehran.
